headline: Bohl Enterprises proposes $10.6 million, 72,000-sq-ft North Toledo manufacturing facility at undeveloped Stickney Avenue site
paragraphs: Bohl Enterprises — a century-old Toledo material-handling and equipment company — has filed plans with the Toledo City Plan Commission to construct a new 72,000-square-foot manufacturing and office facility at 5315 Stickney Ave. in North Toledo, The Blade reported August 4. The proposed investment totals $10.6 million. According to city planning documents, the company intends to consolidate its existing manufacturing and office operations from multiple locations into the new facility. The roughly 21-acre parcel sits south of Shantee Creek and has not been targeted for industrial development since 1974, when City Council denied a special-use permit for a sanitary landfill at the site.

Bohl Equipment Co. — which operates under the Bohl brand — is a Hyster & Yale forklift dealership and crane and lifting equipment provider with roots spanning more than a century in Toledo's industrial sector. The company currently operates a location on W. Laskey Road in Toledo. The Stickney Avenue plan represents the company's expansion of its North Toledo manufacturing footprint; city plan commission review is the next procedural step before construction permitting.
why_it_matters: A $10.6 million private manufacturing investment in a long-dormant North Toledo industrial parcel is the kind of infill industrial activity Toledo EDOs and the city's economic development office track as a signal of reinvestment in legacy manufacturing corridors. The site's 51-year history without development — stretching back to 1974 — makes the proposal notable as a reactivation of underutilized industrial land. If approved and built, the facility consolidates an established Toledo employer on a North Toledo footprint and adds taxable value to a parcel that has generated no commercial activity since before the current generation of city planners.
